members.name: audit-security
members.prompt:
You are auditing a multi-tenant ERP platform for security issues. Two repos, read-only, report findings only — do not edit anything.

Repos:
- /Users/sabiridwan/Projects/zerp/zerp-be (NestJS 9 + GraphQL code-first + Mongoose backend, one process per tenant)
- /Users/sabiridwan/Projects/zerp/zerp-admin (Next.js admin dashboard, one process per tenant)

Known context (from project CLAUDE.md, verify current state — don't assume it's still true):
- zerp-be: `ApGqlAuthorize` decorator in `src/modules/auth/decorators/gql-auth.decorator.ts` reportedly has its guards removed (should be `UseGuards(GqlRolesGuard, GqlClientGuard)`).
- zerp-admin: `requirePermission` in `src/lib/requirePermission.ts` reportedly always returns `true` (should check `getServerSession` + real permission).
- Multi-tenant model: each tenant has its own MongoDB DB. Code should always read `contextSvc.companyId`/`contextSvc.branchId` from context, never hardcode. Look for any query, mutation, or resolver missing tenant scoping — that's a cross-tenant data leak.
- Standard: Resolver → Service → Repository → Schema layering. Resolvers should extend `ApBaseResolver<T>`, use `@ApGqlAuthorize()` + `@AuditMeta()`. No raw Mongoose queries outside repositories.

What to check across BOTH repos:
1. Confirm current state of the two known temp bypasses above (file:line, exact current code).
2. Any other resolver/route missing auth guards or permission checks.
3. Any query/mutation/repository method missing tenant (companyId/branchId) scoping — search for `.find(`, `.findOne(`, aggregation pipelines that don't filter by company/branch.
4. Hardcoded secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials in source (not env/config).
5. JWT handling: token validation, expiry checks, refresh flow — any logic errors (e.g. `<` vs `<=` on expiry).
6. Injection risks: any raw/dynamic Mongo queries built from unsanitized user input; any `eval`, `Function()`, or command execution from user input.
7. CORS, rate limiting, input validation (class-validator usage) gaps on money/auth-sensitive endpoints.
8. zerp-admin: any client-side-only permission check with no server-side enforcement (API routes/resolvers must also check).

Report as a ranked list, most severe first. Each finding: file:path:line, one-sentence description of the vulnerability, concrete exploit scenario (what an attacker/malicious tenant could do), and suggested fix direction. Skip theoretical/low-impact nits — focus on things that are actually exploitable given this is live multi-tenant financial ERP data. Keep total report under 150 lines.

members.name: fix-security
members.prompt:
You are fixing confirmed security audit findings in a multi-tenant ERP. Write real, complete fixes — no TODOs, no placeholders. Do NOT git commit or push; leave changes uncommitted. Do NOT ask questions — if you hit an ambiguity, pick the most conservative correct option and note your decision in your final report.

Repos:
- /Users/sabiridwan/Projects/zerp/zerp-master (Next.js control plane, zync-nextjs standard, `next-auth`)
- /Users/sabiridwan/Projects/zerp/zerp-be (NestJS backend)
- /Users/sabiridwan/Projects/zerp/zerp-admin (Next.js admin dashboard)

## Fix 1 — CRITICAL: zerp-master has no authentication at all
`zerp-master/src/lib/requirePermission.ts` currently always returns `true` with a TODO comment. Routes that call it never call `getServerSession`/`getSessionUser` either — so there's no auth check whatsoever, not even "must be logged in." Affected routes include (verify the exact list yourself, this may not be exhaustive): `pages/api/tenants/index.ts`, `pages/api/tenants/[key].ts`, `pages/api/processes/index.ts`, `pages/api/migrate/index.ts`, `pages/api/build-projects/*`, `pages/api/platform-users/*`, `pages/api/features/[tenantKey].ts`.

Read `zerp-master/src/lib/auth.ts` (or wherever NextAuth options live) to understand the session/user shape and role field. Restore `requirePermission` to:
1. Call `getServerSession` (or equivalent) to get the current user.
2. Return `false` (or throw, matching how callers currently use the return value — check call sites) if there's no session.
3. Check the user's role/permission against whatever permission model zerp-master already has (look for an enum or role field — e.g. ADMIN-only, or a granular permission list — mirror how zerp-admin's `admin-guard.ts` pattern does it if zerp-master has something similar, or check zerp-master's own user/role schema).
4. Update every call site to actually use the real result (if some routes call `requirePermission` but ignore its return value, fix that too — this was found in the audit as part of the bug).

This is the highest-stakes fix in the whole audit — full platform compromise is possible until this is fixed (tenant CRUD, PM2 process control including killing prod processes, and DB migration triggers are all currently open to anyone). Take your time to get it right and verify every affected route actually enforces the check after your fix, not just the shared helper.

## Fix 2 — MEDIUM: zerp-be CORS reflects any origin with credentials enabled
`zerp-be/src/main.ts` around lines 21-25 has `app.enableCors({ origin: true, ..., credentials: true })`. Replace `origin: true` with an explicit allowlist. Check how tenant admin domains are already known to zerp-be at boot (env var, config service, `tenant.domain` from platform DB via `TenantConfigService`, or a `.env` var like `CORS_ORIGINS`/`ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) — use whatever mechanism already exists in this codebase to build the allowlist, matching project conventions. If nothing exists, use an env var (comma-separated list) with a sane local-dev default, and document it in zerp-be's own CLAUDE.md if one exists.

## Fix 3 — HIGH: zerp-admin ESS JWT stored in non-httpOnly cookie
`zerp-admin/src/pages/api/ess/session.ts` (around lines 5-11) sets a cookie named `ess-token` with `httpOnly: false`, containing the full ESS sign-in payload including the JWT `accessToken`. `zerp-admin/src/modules/ess/ApolloClientEss.tsx` (around lines 12-24) then reads it directly out of `document.cookie` on the client to build the GraphQL `Authorization: Bearer` header.

Fix: make the cookie `httpOnly: true`. Since the client-side Apollo link currently needs the raw token to build the Authorization header, you'll need a different way to attach it — options in order of preference: (a) proxy ESS GraphQL calls through a Next.js API route that reads the httpOnly cookie server-side and forwards the request with the Authorization header attached server-side (client never sees the token), or (b) if (a) is too large a refactor for this pass, at minimum make the token itself httpOnly and keep a separate non-sensitive flag cookie (e.g. `ess-authenticated=true`, no token) that client code can check for "is logged in" state, while all actual authenticated GraphQL calls go through a server proxy route. Pick whichever fits the existing ESS module structure with the least disruption, and implement it fully — don't leave it half-done. Check all call sites of `ApolloClientEss` / anywhere else that reads `ess-token` from `document.cookie` and update them consistently.

## After fixing all 3
Run typecheck/build for all three repos (check each `package.json` for the right script — likely `tsc --noEmit` or `npm run build`) and fix any errors your changes introduced. Report back: what you changed (file:line), the exact auth/permission model you wired into zerp-master's requirePermission and why, how you resolved the ESS token exposure, and the verification output (typecheck/build pass/fail) for each repo.

members.name: fix-idor
members.prompt:
You are fixing a confirmed cross-company IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) vulnerability in a multi-tenant gold/jewellery ERP backend. This is correctness-critical, money-adjacent security work. Do NOT git commit or push; leave changes uncommitted. Do NOT ask questions — investigate, decide, act, and log every decision in your report.

Repo: /Users/sabiridwan/Projects/zerp/zerp-be (NestJS 9 + GraphQL code-first + Mongoose)

## The vulnerability
Read `src/core/database/database.repository.ts`. `findById`/`update`/`delete` (and similar direct-by-`_id` operations) only filter by `companyId` when the concrete repository class sets `protected companyScoped = true`. List/page/aggregate queries auto-inject a companyId `$match` via a `companyMatch()`-style helper regardless of this flag, so browsing/listing is already safe — but any direct-by-ID read/update/delete on a repo that never set `companyScoped = true` has NO company isolation at all.

An audit found 68 repos already set `companyScoped = true` (HR, manufacturing, some inventory: warehouse/lot/serial) but 87 repos did not, including these confirmed financially sensitive ones: `finance/account`, `finance/payment`, `finance/transaction`, `finance/taxation`, `finance/note`, `finance/shortcut`, `customer`, `supplier`, `budget`, `subscription`/`plan`/`feature`, `inventory/sales/item`, `inventory/purchase/item`.

Concretely confirmed exploitable: `finance/account.resolver.ts` `updateAccount(_id, ...)`/`deleteAccount(_id)` and `finance/payment.resolver.ts` `updatePaymentEntry(_id, ...)`/`deletePaymentEntry(_id)` take a raw Mongo `_id` with zero companyId check anywhere in the call path — a user in Company A who obtains Company B's `_id` (these leak via exports, audit logs, URLs, support tickets — ObjectIds aren't secret) can read/edit/delete Company B's financial records within the same tenant database.

## Your task
1. First, grep the entire `src/modules/` tree for every repository class extending `AbstractBaseRepository` and determine the full, exact list of repos where `companyScoped` is NOT set to `true` (don't just trust the audit's list — verify it yourself, it may be stale or incomplete).
2. Before changing anything: check whether ANY code path in this codebase deliberately relies on cross-company access for a legitimate reason — e.g. a superadmin/platform-level role that needs to see across companies within a tenant, a consolidated/group financial report, or an inter-company transfer feature. Search for terms like "consolidated", "cross-company", "superadmin", "allCompanies", "group report" in resolvers/services. If you find a genuine legitimate cross-company code path, do NOT break it — instead make it explicit (e.g. an explicit `{ skipCompanyScope: true }` param or a dedicated method) rather than relying on the current implicit "just didn't opt in" gap, and leave a clear comment explaining why that specific path is intentionally unscoped.
3. For every other repo without a legitimate reason to skip scoping, set `protected companyScoped = true`. Prioritize the confirmed list above first (finance/*, customer, supplier, budget, subscription/plan/feature, inventory/sales/item, inventory/purchase/item), then sweep the rest.
4. Read `database.repository.ts` carefully to confirm what `companyScoped = true` actually changes in `findById`/`update`/`delete` — make sure the company id it filters by is sourced correctly (from request context / `contextSvc.companyId`, per this project's multi-tenant convention — see root CLAUDE.md: "always read `contextSvc.companyId`/`contextSvc.branchId`, never hardcode").
5. After flipping the flag on a batch of repos, there's real risk of breaking legitimate same-company operations if the context's companyId isn't being threaded through correctly on some call paths (e.g. background jobs, system-triggered writes with no request context). Check for any resolver/service call site that invokes `findById`/`update`/`delete` on a newly-scoped repo from a context where `contextSvc.companyId` might not be reliably set (cron jobs, webhooks, migration scripts) and fix those call sites to pass the company id explicitly if needed, rather than letting them silently fail once scoping is enforced.

## Verification
Run zerp-be's typecheck/build (check `package.json` for the script) after your changes. If there are existing tests (`*.spec.ts`) covering `finance/`, `customer`, `supplier`, `budget`, or `subscription` repos/services, run those specifically and fix any failures caused by your change (a test that was relying on cross-company data leakage to pass is a good sign your fix works, but a test failing because company context wasn't set up in the test at all needs the test fixture fixed, not the security fix reverted).

## Report back
- Exact count and list of repos you flipped to `companyScoped = true`, grouped by module.
- Any repos you deliberately left unscoped and why (the legitimate cross-company case, if any was found).
- Any call sites you had to fix because they didn't reliably have `contextSvc.companyId` available.
- Verification output (typecheck/build/test pass or fail).

members.name: fix-finance
members.prompt:
You are fixing confirmed accounting/finance bugs in a multi-tenant gold/jewellery ERP backend. This is correctness-critical money code. Do NOT git commit or push; leave changes uncommitted. Do NOT ask questions — investigate, decide, act, log decisions in your report.

Repo: /Users/sabiridwan/Projects/zerp/zerp-be (NestJS 9, finance module at src/modules/finance)

## Fix 1 (BOOKS-WRONG, highest priority) — duplicate self-cancelling tax leg on Note/Payment entries
Look at `finance/note/note.service.ts` (around lines 804-856) and `finance/transaction/transaction.service.ts` (around lines 75-162). Both leg-builder methods (`addAccountTransaction` / `addMainAccountTransaction` or similarly named) pass the same `taxId`/`taxIds`/`taxInclusive` info to `transacSvc.create()` (in `AccountTransactionService`), and `AccountTransactionService.create()` independently fires its own `createTaxEntries()` for each leg — so a single taxed Note or Payment entry ends up posting TWO opposite-direction tax legs (which cancel each other out on the Tax Payable/Receivable account, netting it to zero regardless of the real tax amount) plus grossed-up principal legs. Net effect: tax liability is silently wrong in every report that reads the Tax Payable account, and the entry still "balances" (Dr=Cr) so nothing catches it.

Trace the actual call graph yourself to confirm exactly where the double-posting happens (the audit's line numbers are a starting point, may have drifted). Fix so tax is computed and posted exactly once per entry — likely means removing the duplicate `createTaxEntries()` call from one of the two paths (either the leg-builder should stop building its own tax-aware leg and let `AccountTransactionService.create()` own tax entirely, or vice versa — pick whichever matches how a non-buggy entry type like Journal already does it; check `journal.service.ts` for the correct reference pattern since journal entries apparently don't have this bug).

## Fix 2 (BOOKS-WRONG) — posted payments freely editable
`finance/payment/payment.resolver.ts` around line 106, `updatePaymentEntry` mutation is missing the `@GuardPostedEntry` decorator that's present on the equivalent journal/note/cashbook/trade/contra resolvers. `finance/payment/payment.service.ts` `update()` method (around lines 230-280) also has zero status check. Add `@GuardPostedEntry` (or whatever the exact decorator/guard name is — check a sibling resolver like journal or note for the exact import and usage) to `updatePaymentEntry` (and `deletePaymentEntry` if it has the same gap — check). This will change behavior: a POSTED payment can no longer be edited/deleted directly, matching every other entry type. That's the intended fix.

## Fix 3 (CONTROL-GAP) — accountBalanced() blind for most entry kinds
`finance/account/account.service.ts` `accountBalanced()` (around lines 623-644) is called after 60+ finance/inventory/asset writes but only sums `JournalEntry`/`AdvanceTransaction`/`LoanRepayment` company-wide — for ~16 other entry kinds it checks an unrelated aggregate and always reports "balanced" regardless of what was just posted, so none of those 16 kinds get any Dr=Cr integrity check at all. Fix by either (a) scoping the balance check to the specific entry just written (pass the entry id/type in and sum only its own legs), which is more correct and avoids company-wide false negatives masking a single bad entry, or (b) extending the kind-list to cover all ~16 other entry kinds if per-entry scoping is too large a change for this pass. Prefer (a) if you can identify all call sites cleanly; fall back to (b) and note it in your report if (a) turns out to require touching too many unrelated call sites.

## Fix 4 (DEBT) — console.log spam
`account.service.ts` line ~642 has a `console.log` of Dr/Cr totals on every `accountBalanced()` call (60+ call sites trigger it). Remove it, or replace with whatever this project's actual logger is (check for a `Logger` import from `@nestjs/common` used elsewhere in the file/module) at `debug`/`verbose` level, not `console.log`.

## Fix 5 (DEBT) — silent transaction no-op
`services/service.ts` (find the actual path — likely `src/core/services/service.ts` or similar, around lines 14-26 and 116-124) — `withRetryTransaction` silently no-ops (skips using a real Mongo session/transaction) unless env var `mongodb_transaction_enabled === "true"` (or a deprecated misspelled variant is also checked — find and note the exact variant). Add a boot-time assertion (e.g. in the module's `onModuleInit` or main bootstrap) that throws/fails startup if this env var is not explicitly `"true"` when `NODE_ENV`/`app_env` is not `local`/`development` — so this can never silently be off in a real deployment.

## Fix 6 (DEBT) — inconsistent magic-number tolerance
`journal.service.ts` line ~82 uses `0.001` and `account.service.ts` line ~642 uses `0.01` as balance-tolerance magic numbers. Extract a single shared constant (e.g. `LEDGER_BALANCE_TOLERANCE`) in an appropriate shared location (a constants file in the finance module, or wherever similar shared constants already live in this codebase), and use it in both places. Pick one value — `0.01` is more likely correct for currency rounding at 2 decimal places; use your judgment based on what currencies/decimal precision this ERP handles (check schema for currency/decimal fields) and note your choice.

## After fixing
Run zerp-be's typecheck/build and any existing `*.spec.ts` tests covering `finance/note`, `finance/transaction`, `finance/payment`, `finance/account`, `finance/journal`. Fix any failures your changes cause.

## Report back
For each of the 6 fixes: what you changed (file:line), why, and any judgment calls you made (especially fix 1's exact mechanism and fix 3's approach a vs b). Include verification output.

members.name: fix-admin-high
members.prompt:
You are fixing confirmed bugs in a Next.js admin dashboard (zerp-admin) for a multi-tenant gold/jewellery ERP. Follow the project's existing patterns exactly. Do NOT git commit or push; leave changes uncommitted. Do NOT ask questions — pick the most sensible option matching existing code patterns and log your decision.

Repo: /Users/sabiridwan/Projects/zerp/zerp-admin (Next.js pages-router, `src/pages` + `src/modules`)

House standard for this repo (zync-nextjs, adapted for pages-router here): component → `<Feature>Context` → `gql/query.ts` → Apollo. Every module exposes `use<Feature>Query()` wrapping `useMutation`/`useLazyQuery`; only `context.tsx` calls it. Components use `use<Feature>State()` only, never call GraphQL/axios/fetch directly. After any mutation, the context triggers `reload()`/refetch.

## Fix 1 (HIGH) — POS split-payment cash amount is cosmetic
File: `src/modules/pos/terminal/pos-payment-modal.tsx`. In SPLIT payment mode, the "Cash Amount" input (around line 218) is bound to state `cashTendered`, but the actual charge logic (`handleCharge`, around line 87) computes the real cash portion as `splitCash = Math.max(0, total - bankAmount)` — it never reads `cashTendered` when submitting. The validation (`isValid`/`shortfall`, around lines 61-70) checks `cashTendered + bankAmount` against total, which has no relationship to what's actually submitted (`splitCash + bankAmount` always trivially equals `total`). A cashier can type any cash figure, see it validate as correct, and the till silently records a different cash/bank split than what they entered.

DECISION (already made — implement this, don't reconsider): make the cash input the real source of truth. Cashier types the cash amount; bank amount is derived as the remainder (`bankAmount = total - cashTendered`, clamped to >= 0). Remove the dead/misleading validation that checks `cashTendered + bankAmount` and instead validate that `cashTendered <= total` (and handle the case where cashier wants a pure-bank payment by typing 0 cash). Update `handleCharge` to submit the real typed `cashTendered` as the cash leg and the derived remainder as the bank leg. Also replace the raw `<input type="number">` for cash with `ApNumberInput` (check imports of `ApNumberInput` elsewhere in this repo, e.g. `src/frontend/components/ap/` or wherever this repo's shared inputs live) to match convention — check how other numeric POS inputs in this same file/module already use it, if any.

## Fix 2 (HIGH) — deleteMaster does nothing
File: `src/modules/master/context.tsx`, `deleteMaster` function (around lines 127-148). Current code: an optimistic-update filter callback that never actually returns `false` for the matched item (so it can't filter anything), whose result is discarded anyway; then a flat top-level `filter` on `master` state that can't reach nested `children` arrays; and a recursive children-filter that compares `c._id !== m._id` where `m` is the wrong reference (compares child to its own parent, not to the deleted item's id). Compare with sibling `createMaster`/`updateMaster` in the same file, which both call `fetchMaster()` after their mutation succeeds. Fix: after a successful `deleteMaster` mutation, call `fetchMaster()` (with whatever args/filter state those siblings already pass) instead of the broken manual state manipulation. Remove the dead filter code.

## Fix 3 (HIGH) — workflow approval-config page can never show existing rows

## Fix 1 (CRITICAL) — payroll re-run orphans posted GL journal, causing double-counted expense
`zerp-be/src/modules/hr/payroll/payroll.service.ts` around line 1255. Flow: payroll gets APPROVED → posted to GL as journal J1 (`journalEntryId` set) → operator re-runs the payroll (currently allowed; only PAID/CANCELLED statuses are blocked from re-run, per the check around line 844) → the re-run code nulls `journalEntryId` WITHOUT reversing/discarding the previously-posted journal J1 → J1 is now orphaned in the GL, permanently posted and never reversed → when the re-run is later posted, it creates a NEW journal J2 → the GL now carries the payroll expense TWICE (once via orphaned J1, once via J2).

There's already a correct pattern for this exact problem: `cancelPayroll` (around line 2131) calls `discardExistingJournal` before doing its own status change. Fix the re-run path (around line 1255) to call the same `discardExistingJournal` (or whatever it's actually named — verify) BEFORE nulling `journalEntryId`, so the previously-posted journal is properly reversed/discarded instead of orphaned. `zerp-be/src/modules/hr/employee-lifecycle/employee-lifecycle.service.ts` around lines 108-119, `deactivateEmployees` only sets `accountStatus: DEACTIVATED` — it never writes `resignDate`. Payroll proration keys entirely on `resignDate` (`payroll.service.ts:418`, `employee/employee.service.ts:414`) — so a terminated employee gets a FULL MONTH of pay in their exit month instead of a prorated amount. Also `addEmployees` (around line 394, likely in `payroll.service.ts` or a payroll-run-building service — find the exact location) has no `accountStatus` filter, so deactivated employees aren't even excluded from being added to a new payroll run at all. Also Borang E's `ceasedEmployees` (`borang-e.service.ts:70`) counts based on `resignDate`, so a leaver is currently missing from the statutory Form E entirely.

(b) Find and fix the `addEmployees` payroll-run-building step (around the referenced line 394) to exclude employees whose `accountStatus` is `DEACTIVATED` (or whose `resignDate` is before the payroll period, if that's a more correct filter given how proration already uses `resignDate` — use whichever check is consistent with how the rest of the payroll engine already reads `resignDate` for proration, so a leaver either gets correctly prorated for their exit month, or excluded from subsequent runs, not double-counted either way).

Additionally/separately, check `zerp-master/pm2/scripts/start.js` around lines 130-135 to see if `tenant_country` (or the equivalent `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` var) is being injected into the admin process's env at boot — if it's not being injected at all, fix `start.js` to inject it from the tenant record as a defense-in-depth belt-and-suspenders fix alongside the GraphQL-based runtime fix (both fixes together close this properly — build-time injection alone isn't sufithe root cause since a stale build could still be running).
